info.description:
The HTTP API behind the Pursuit dashboard and the `pursuit` CLI. Agents should prefer the CLI: `pursuit schema <command>` describes one command. The short agent guide is [/llms.txt](/llms.txt).

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer pst_...`. A token holds the scopes `read`, `write`, and `approve`. `write` does not include `approve`, and only `approve` can move an application toward submission. Tokens, scopes, and OAuth login are in [/auth.md](/auth.md).

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "details"}}`. 400 is validation, 401 a missing or bad token, 403 a missing scope, 404 not found, 409 a version or cap conflict.

## Writes

Every write accepts `Idempotency-Key`, which replays a successful response, and `X-Dry-Run: true` (or `?dry_run=true`), which validates and writes nothing. A dry run answers `{"dry_run": true, "hint", "data"}` instead of the response shown. Creates answer 201. Updates and deletes of versioned records take `version` in the body, the query, or `If-Match`.

## Pagination

Lists answer `{"data": [...], "page": {"limit", "has_more", "next_cursor", "total"}}`. They take `limit` (1-200) and `cursor`; pass `page.next_cursor` back unchanged until `has_more` is false. `fields=id,company` trims each record to those fields. `POST /v1/batch` runs up to 100 requests in one call.

## Webhooks

A registered webhook receives every new event as a POST; see **Webhooks** at the end of this page for the payload.

post.description: RFC 8628 device authorization for `pursuit auth login --device`. Scope is space or comma separated, each exactly read or write, default read write; anything else (approve, APPROVE, Read) is invalid_scope: OAuth never grants approve. client_id is at most 64 characters. Limited to 10 starts a minute per client IP (429 slow_down). Device codes last 10 minutes; poll /v1/auth/token no faster than interval. There is no verification_uri_complete: the human types the code.

WebAuthn, usernameless. Body {}. PublicKey is for PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON with no allowCredentials, so nothing reveals which accounts exist. The challenge is single-use and lasts 5 minutes. 404 when passkeys are off (PURSUIT_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID unset). Requires Content-Type application/json and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or a matching Origin. Begin and finish together are limited to 20 a minute per client IP (429).

Body is the browser's PublicKeyCredential.toJSON(). Verifies challenge, origin, RP ID, signature, user verification and sign count, then mints a pst_ login token (name login, read,write,approve) into the httpOnly pursuit_session cookie and answers like GET /v1/me. Never creates a user: an unknown, removed or replayed passkey is 401. Same-origin JSON only.

post.description: RFC 7009 token revocation. Holding the token is the authority; unknown tokens still return 200.

delete.description: Clear the pursuit_session cookie and revoke it when sign-in minted it (token name login). Any other token stays valid; revoke it with POST /v1/auth/revoke. Same-origin only.

post.description: Verify a token (pst_, or a Better Auth JWT exchanged for a pst_ login token) and store the pst_ token in the httpOnly pursuit_session cookie, then answer like GET /v1/me. Requires Content-Type application/json and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or a matching Origin. Agents send Authorization: Bearer instead.

OAuth2 token endpoint. grant_type=authorization_code takes code, code_verifier (PKCE S256), redirect_uri, client_id; codes are single-use and last 60 seconds. grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code takes device_code, client_id and answers authorization_pending, slow_down, expired_token, or access_denied until approved. The access_token is a normal pst_ API token.
